subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper sold an item at 20% gain , Had he bought it ₹50 cheaper and sold it at the same price. he would have gained 25%. Find the cost price of the item (in ₹)
solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper sold an item at 20% gain

**Concept used:**

Selling price = Cost price × (100 + profit)%

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the item be 100a

So, selling price = 100a + 120%

⇒ 120a

Now,

In the 2nd case selling price is the same

So, the selling price of the 2nd case = 120a

According to the question,

120a = 125% of cost price [For 2nd selling]

⇒ 120a/125 = 1% of the cost price

⇒ (120a/125) × 100 = The cost price

⇒ 96a = The cost price [New cost price]

Here,

100a - 96a = 50

⇒ 4a = 50

⇒ a = 50/4 = 12.5

So, actual cost price = 100 × 12.5

⇒ Rs. 1250

**∴ The cost price of the item (in ₹) is 1250.**
